me:2015:q5-s2.question: Three vendors were asked to supply a very high precision component. The respective probabilities of their meeting the strict design specifications are 0.8, 0.7 and 0.5.  Each vendor supplies one component. The probability that out of total three components supplied by the vendors, at least one will meet the design specification is ___________

me:2015:q6-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 6
me:2015:q6-s2.question: A small ball of mass 1 kg moving with a velocity of 12 m/s undergoes a direct central impact with a stationary ball of mass 2 kg. The impact is perfectly elastic. The speed (in m/s) of 2 kg mass ball after the impact will be ____________

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mechanics - Impulse and Momentum, Energy Formulations
detailed_solution.markdown: 1. Conserving linear momentum $$\begin{aligned} 1 \times 12 &=1 \times V_{1}+2 \times V_{2} \\ 12 &=V_{1}+2 V_{2}\qquad \ldots(i) \end{aligned}$$ 2. Velocity of approach = Velocity of seperation $12-0=v_{2}-v_{1}$ $V_{2}-V_{1}=12 \qquad \ldots(ii)$ From (i) and (ii), we get $v_{2}=8 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **8** (acceptable range: [7.8, 8.2]).

me:2015:q7-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 7
me:2015:q7-s2.question: A rod is subjected to a uni-axial load within linear elastic limit. When the change in the stress is   200 MPa, the change in the strain is 0.001. If the Poisson's ratio of the rod is 0.3, the modulus of rigidity (in GPa) is ________________

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Stress-strain Relationship and Elastic Constants
detailed_solution.markdown: With in linear elastic limit $\sigma=E \in$ $E \rightarrow \text{ slope of } \sigma \text{ vs }\in \text{ curve}$ $$\begin{aligned} E &=\frac{d \sigma}{d \epsilon}=\frac{200}{0.001}=200 \mathrm{GPa} \\ E &=2 G[1+\mu] \\ G &=\frac{E}{2(1+\mu)}=\frac{200}{2(1+0.3)}=\frac{100}{1.3} \\ &=76.9230 \mathrm{GPa} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **77** (acceptable range: [76, 78]).

me:2015:q10-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 10
me:2015:q10-s2.question: In a spring-mass system, the mass is m and the spring constant is k. The critical damping coefficient of the system is 0.1 kg/s. In another spring-mass system, the mass is 2m and the spring constant is 8k. The critical damping coefficient (in kg/s) of this system is ____________

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \xi &=\frac{C}{2 \sqrt{m k}} \\ C &=2 \xi \sqrt{m k} \\ \frac{C_{2}}{C_{1}} &=\frac{2 \xi_{2} \sqrt{m_{2} k_{2}}}{2 \xi_{1} \sqrt{m_{1} k_{1}}} \\ \frac{C_{2}}{0.1} &=\frac{2 \times 1 \sqrt{2 m \times 8 k}}{2 \times 1 \sqrt{m \times k}} \\ C_{2} &=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.4** (acceptable range: [0.38, 0.42]).

me:2015:q11-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 11
me:2015:q11-s2.question: The uniaxial yield stress of a material is 300 MPa. According to von Mises criterion, the shear yield stress (in MPa) of the material is _______

$$\begin{aligned} \tau_{y} &=\frac{\sigma_{y}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ &=\frac{300}{\sqrt{3}}=173.1 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **173** (acceptable range: [171, 175]).

me:2015:q12-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 12
me:2015:q12-s2.question: If the fluid velocity for a potential flow is given by $V(x,y)=u(x,y)i+v(x,y)j$  with usual notations, then the slope of the potential line at $(x,y)$  is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} d \phi&=\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x} d x+\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial y} d y\\ \therefore \qquad \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x}&=-u\\ \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial y}&=-v \\ \therefore \qquad d \phi&=-u d x-v d y \\ \text { If } \phi&=\text { constant, } d \phi=0 \\ \therefore \quad\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{\phi}&=-\frac{u}{v} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:q21-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 21
me:2015:q21-s2.question: The primary mechanism of material removal in electrochemical machining (ECM) is

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Governing Mechanism of Electrochemical Machining:**
  - Electrochemical Machining (ECM) is an advanced non-traditional machining process based on Faraday's laws of electrolysis.
  - The metallic workpiece is connected as the **anode** ($+$) and the shaped tool is connected as the **cathode** ($-$) with a fast-flowing electrolyte (e.g., aqueous $\text{NaCl}$ solution) in a microscopic inter-electrode gap ($0.1 - 0.5\text{ mm}$).
  - As DC current passes through the cell, anodic metal atoms lose valence electrons and dissolve directly into the electrolyte as hydrated ions:
    $$M \rightarrow M^{z+} + z e^-$$
  - Hence, material removal occurs strictly via controlled anodic **ionic dissolution** on an atomic scale, resulting in zero tool wear, no thermal damage, and no residual stresses.

- **Distractor Analysis:**
  - **Chemical corrosion:** Refers to uncontrolled spontaneous chemical degradation.
  - **Etching:** Refers to chemical machining (CHM) using acid/base etchants without applied external electric fields.
  - **Spark erosion:** The material removal mechanism of Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM), where localized thermal melting occurs via pulsed spark plasma discharges.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (ionic dissolution)**.

me:2015:q23-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 23
me:2015:q23-s2.question: During the development of a product, an entirely new process plan is made based on design logic, examination of geometry and tolerance information. This type of process planning is known as

detailed_solution.concept: Industrial Engineering - Production Planning and Control
detailed_solution.markdown:
A generative manufacturing process different from a traditional manufacturing process develops a product with the addition of material instead of removal of the excess material as in case of a traditional manufacturing process.

In the generative manufacturing process, plans are generated by means of decision logic, formulas, technology algorithm and geometry-based data to perform uniquely the many processing decision for converting a part from raw material to a finished state.

There are two major components of a generative process planning system.

A geometry-based coding scheme.

Process knowledge in the form of decision logic and data.

Geometry-based coding scheme:

The objective of a geometric based coding scheme is to define all geometric features for all process related surfaces together with feature dimensions, locations, tolerances and the surface finish desired on the features.

Advantage of Generative Manufacturing Process:

No tools and fixtures are required.

No restriction on geometry of the part shape exists.

Composite parts and assemblies can be produced in one go.

Small batch production of complex parts is economically viable.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:q27-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 27
me:2015:q27-s2.question: The surface integral $\iint_{s} (1/\pi) (9xi-3yj)\cdot n dS$  over the sphere given by $x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=9$   is ______

me:2015:q28-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 28
me:2015:q28-s2.question:
Consider the following differential equation:
$\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} t}= -5y$ ; initial condition:y=2 at t=0.
The value of y at t = 3 is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \frac{d y}{d t} &=-5 y \\ \int \frac{d y}{y} &=-\int 5 d t \\ \ln y &=-5 t+C \\ \text{at} \qquad t &=0 \\ y&=2 \\ \ln 2&=C \\ \text{So,} \quad \ln y&=-5 t+\ln 2 \\ \ln \frac{y}{2} &=-5 t \\ \frac{y}{2} &=e^{-5 t} \\ y &=2 e^{-5 t} \\ at \qquad t &=3 \\ y&=2 e^{-15} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2015:q30-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 30
me:2015:q30-s2.question:
The initial velocity of an object is 40 m/s. The acceleration a of the object is given by the following expression:
a=-0.1v,

where v is the instantaneous velocity of the object. The velocity of the object after 3 seconds will be _______

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} u &=40 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ a &=-0.1 \mathrm{v} \\ V &=? \\ t &=3 \mathrm{s} \\ a &=\frac{d v}{d t}=-0.1 \mathrm{v} \\ \int_{40}^{v} \frac{d v}{v} &=\int_{0}^{3}-0.1 d t \\\;[\ln v]_{40}^{v} &=-0.1[t] \\ \ln v-\ln 40 &=-0.1[3.0]=-0.3 \\ \ln v &=\ln 40-0.3 \\ \ln v &=3.38887 \\\text{or}\qquad v &=e^{3.38887}=29.63 \mathrm{m} \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **29.6** (acceptable range: [29.5, 29.7]).

me:2015:q31-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 31
me:2015:q31-s2.question: A cantilever beam OP is connected to another beam PQ with a pin joint as shown in the figure. A load of 10 kN is applied at the mid-point of PQ. The magnitude of bending moment (in kN-m) at fixed end O is

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Shear-force and Bending Moment Diagrams
detailed_solution.markdown: At hinge moment releases Taking summation of all forces $P_{V}+R_{Q}=10$ Taking moment of all forces about Q $M=\underset{clockwise}{\left(P_{V} \times 1\right)}-\underset{anticlockwise}{(10 \times 0.5)}$ At equilibrium M=0 $$\begin{array}{rl} \therefore \quad 0 & =\left(P_{V} \times 1\right)-5 \\ P_{V} & =5 \mathrm{kN} \end{array}$$ Summation of all vertical forces is zero. $\therefore \quad O_{V}+P_{V}=0$ Summation of Moments of all forces at equilibrium is zero. $\therefore \quad\underset{clockwise}{+M}+\underset{clockwise}{P_{v}\times 2}=0$ $\therefore M=-P_{V} \times 2$ $\text{where}\quad P_{V}=-5 \mathrm{kN}$ $\therefore M=10 \mathrm{kN}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2015:q33-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 33
me:2015:q33-s2.question: A cantilever beam with square cross-section of 6 mm side is subjected to a load of 2 kN normal to the top surface as shown in the figure. The Young's modulus of elasticity of the material of the beam is 210 GPa. The magnitude of slope (in radian) at Q (20 mm from the fixed end) is ________

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Bending of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown: Slope $\theta_{Q}-\theta_{0}=\frac{1}{E I}[\text { Area of diagram till } Q]$ Area of diagram till " Q " $\left[\frac{1}{2} \times 100 \times 2 \times 10^{5}\right]-\left[\frac{1}{2} \times 80 \times y\right]$ Calculating; y from properties of similar triangles. $$\begin{aligned} \frac{y}{2 \times 10^{5}} &=\frac{80}{100} \\ y &=160,000 \mathrm{Nmm} \end{aligned}$$ Area of diagram till Q $$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow\left[1 / 2 \times 100 \times 2 \times 10^{5}\right]-[1 / 2 \times 80 \times 160,000] \\ =3600000 \mathrm{N} . \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ \theta_{Q}=\frac{1}{210 \times 10^{3} \times I} \times 3600000 \\ I=\frac{b d^{3}}{12}=\frac{b^{4}}{12}=\frac{b^{4}}{12}=108 \mathrm{mm}^{4} \\ \theta_{Q}=\frac{1}{210 \times 10^{3} \times 108} \times 3600000 \\ =0.1587 \mathrm{rad} \end{array}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.16** (acceptable range: [0.15, 0.17]).

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2015:q35-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 35
me:2015:q35-s2.question: In a certain slider-crank mechanism, lengths of crank and connecting rod are equal. If the crank rotates with a uniform angular speed of 14 rad/s and the crank length is 300 mm, the maximum acceleration of the slider (in m/$s^{2}$) is ___________

detailed_solution.markdown:
$a=r \omega^{2}\left[\cos \theta+\frac{\cos 2 \theta}{n}\right]$

$\text{at} \quad \theta=0$

$$\begin{aligned} a &\Rightarrow a_{\max } \\ a_{\max } &=r \omega^{2}\left[1+\frac{1}{n}\right] \\ n &=\frac{l}{r}=1 \\ a_{\max } &=2 r \omega^{2}=2 \times 0.3 \times 14^{2} \\ &=117.6 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **117.5** (acceptable range: [115, 120]).

me:2015:q36-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 36
me:2015:q36-s2.question: A single-degree-freedom spring-mass system is subjected to a sinusoidal force of 10 N amplitude and frequency $\omega$ along the axis of the spring. The stiffness of the spring is 150 N/m, damping factor is 0.2 and the undamped natural frequency is 10$\omega$.  At steady state, the amplitude of vibration (in m) is approximately

detailed_solution.markdown:
$A=\frac{F_{0} / s}{\sqrt{\left[1-\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}\right]^{2}+\left(2 \xi \frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}}}$

data given

$$\begin{array}{c} F=10 \mathrm{N} \\ S=150 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ \frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}=\frac{\omega}{10 \omega}=0.1 \\ \varepsilon=0.2 \\ \Rightarrow A=\frac{10 / 150}{\sqrt{\left[1-(0.1)^{2}\right]^{2}+[2 \times 0.2 \times 0.1]^{2}}}=0.07 \mathrm{m} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:q37-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 37
me:2015:q37-s2.question: A hollow shaft of 1 m length is designed to transmit a power of 30 kW at 700 rpm. The maximum permissible angle of twist in the shaft is $1^{\circ}$. The inner diameter of the shaft is 0.7 times the outer diameter. The modulus of rigidity is 80 GPa. The outside diameter (in mm) of the shaft is__________

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Torsion of Shafts
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data,

$$\begin{aligned} P &=30 \mathrm{kW} \\ N &=700 \mathrm{rpm} \\ \frac{2 \pi \mathrm{NT}}{60} &=30 \times 10^{3}=P\\ \text { or } \quad T&=409.25 \mathrm{Nm} \\ \theta=& \frac{T L}{G J} \\ \therefore \frac{1 \times \pi}{180}&=\frac{409.25 \times 10^{3} \times 10^{3} \times 32}{\pi \times\left(d_{0}\right)^{4}\left(1-0.7^{4}\right) \times 80 \times 10^{3}} \\ \text { or } \quad d_{0}&= 44.5212  \mathrm{mm}  \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **44** (acceptable range: [43, 45]).

me:2015:q38-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 38
me:2015:q38-s2.question: A hollow shaft ($d_{o}$ = 2$d_{i}$  where $d_{o}$ and $d_{i}$ are the outer and inner diameters respectively) needs to transmit 20 kW power at 3000 RPM. If the maximum permissible shear stress is 30 MPa, $d_{o}$  is

detailed_solution.concept: Strength of Materials - Torsion of Shafts
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data,

$$\begin{aligned} d_{o} &=2 d_{i} \\ k &=\frac{d_{i}}{d_{o}}=0.5 \\ P &=20 \mathrm{kW} \\ N &=3000 \mathrm{RPM} \\ \frac{2 \pi \mathrm{NT}}{60} &=P \\ \text{or}\quad T &=\frac{60 \times 20 \times 10^{3}}{2 \pi \times 3000}\\ \Rightarrow & 63.66197 \mathrm{Nm} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \tau_{\max } &=\frac{16 T}{\pi d_{0}^{3}\left(1-k^{4}\right)} \\ 30 &=\frac{16 \times 63.66197 \times 10^{3}}{\pi \times d_{0}^{3}\left(1-0.5^{4}\right)} \\ \text { or } \quad d_{0} &=22.59 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$

me:2015:q39-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 39
me:2015:q39-s2.question: The total emissive power of a surface is 500 W/$m^{2}$ at a temperature $T_{1}$ and 1200 W/$m^{2}$ at a temperature $T_{2}$, where the temperatures are in Kelvin. Assuming the emissivity of the surface to be  constant, the ratio of the temperatures $\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
E(emmisive power) $\propto T^{4} \quad(\because \in=\text { Constant })$

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{E_{1}}{E_{2}}&=\left(\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}\right)^{4} \\ \text{or} \quad \frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}&=\left(\frac{500}{1200}\right)^{1 / 4}=0.803 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2015:q40-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 40
me:2015:q40-s2.question: The head loss for a laminar incompressible flow through a horizontal circular pipe is $h_{1}$. Pipe length and fluid remaining the same, if the average flow velocity doubles and the pipe diameter reduces to half its previous value, the head loss is$h_{2}$ . The ratio $\frac{h_{2}}{h_{1}}$  is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text { Head loss: } & h_{f}=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u} L}{\rho g D^{2}} \\ & h_{1}=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u} L}{\rho g D^{2}}\\ \text{and }\quad h_{2}&=\frac{32 \mu \times 2 \bar{u} L}{\rho g(D / 2)^{2}} \\ &=\frac{32 \mu 2 \bar{u} L \times 4}{\rho g D^{2}}=\frac{8 \times 32 \mu \pi L}{\rho g D^{2}} \\ \frac{h_{2}}{h_{1}} &=\frac{8 \times 32 \mu \bar{u} L}{\rho g D^{2}} \times \frac{\rho g D^{2}}{32 \mu \bar{U} L}=8 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

me:2015:q41-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 41
me:2015:q41-s2.question: For a fully developed laminar flow of water (dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa-s) through a pipe of radius 5 cm, the axial pressure gradient is -10 Pa/m. The magnitude of axial velocity (in m/s) at a radial location of 0.2 cm is _______

primary.subtopicLabel: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics - Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \mu &=0.001 \mathrm{Pa}-\mathrm{s} \\ R &=5 \mathrm{cm}=0.05 \mathrm{m} \\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial x} &=-10 \mathrm{Pa} / \mathrm{m} \\ r &=0.2 \mathrm{cm}=0.002 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ For incompressible laminar flow throughpipe Local velocity, $$\begin{aligned} u &=-\frac{1}{4 \mu} \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\left[R^{2}-r^{2}\right] \\ &=-\frac{1}{4 \times 0.001} \times(-10)\left[(0.05)^{2}-(0.002)^{2}\right] \\ &=6.24 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **6.25** (acceptable range: [6.2, 6.3]).

me:2015:q42-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 42
me:2015:q42-s2.question: A balanced counterflow heat exchanger has a surface area of 20 $m^{2}$  and overall heat transfer coefficient of 20 W/$m^{2}$ -K. Air ($C_{p}$ =1000 J/kg-K) entering at 0.4 kg/s and 280 K is to be preheated by the air leaving the system at 0.4 kg/s and 300 K. The outlet temperature (in K) of the preheated air is

detailed_solution.markdown: Given data: $$\begin{aligned} A&=20 \mathrm{m}^{3} ; \quad U=20 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} ; \quad c_{p h}=1000 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{K} \\ m_{c}&=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad T_{c 1}=280 \mathrm{K} ; \quad m_{h}=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ T_{h 2}&=300 \mathrm{K} ; \quad T_{c 2}=? \end{aligned}$$ By energy balance, Heat lost by hot fluid = Heat gained by cold fluid $m_{h} c_{p h}\left(T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}\right)=m_{c} c_{p c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right)$ $\text{or }\quad T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}=T_{c 2}-T_{c 1} \quad \because m_{h} c_{p h}=m_{c} c_{p c}$ $$\begin{aligned} T_{h 1}-T_{c 2} &=T_{h 2}-T_{c 1} \\ \theta_{1} &=\theta_{2} \\ \text { If } \theta_{1}&=\theta_{2} \text { , then } L M T D=\theta_{1}=\theta_{2} \\ Q &=A U L M T D \\ Q &=A U \times \theta_{1} \\ &=20 \times 20 \times\left(T_{h 2}-T_{c 1}\right) \\ &=400(300-280)=8000 \mathrm{kW} \\ \text{also }\quad Q&=m_{c} c_{p c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right) \\ \therefore \quad 8000 &=0.4 \times 1000\left(T_{c 2}-280\right) \\ 20&=T_{c 2}-280 \\ \text{or}\quad T_{c 2}&=300^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}$$ Alternatively: Given data: $A=20 \mathrm{m}^{3} ; U=20 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} ; \quad$ $c_{\mathrm{ph}}=1000 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK}$ $m_{c}=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad T_{c 1}=280 \mathrm{K} ; \quad m_{h}=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}$ $T_{h 2}=300 \mathrm{K} ; \quad T_{c 2}=?$ By energy balance, Heat lost by hot fluid = Heat gained by cold fluid $m_{h} c_{p h}\left(T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}\right)=m_{c} c_{p c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right)$ $$\begin{aligned} \text { or } T_{h 1}-T_{h 2} &=T_{c 2}-T_{c 1} \qquad \because m_{h} c_{p h}=m_{c} c_{p c} \\ T_{h 1}-300 &=T_{c 2}-280 \\ T_{h 1}-T_{c 2} &=300-280 \qquad \ldots(1) \\ T_{h 1}-T_{c 2} &=20 \\ \epsilon&=\frac{N T U}{N T U+1} \quad[ \text{For balancing heat exchanger}]\\ \frac{T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}}{T_{h 1}-T_{c 1}} &=\frac{1}{1+1} \\ \frac{T_{h 1}-300}{T_{h 1}-280} &=\frac{1}{2} \\ 2 T_{h 1}-600 &=T_{h 1}-280 \\ T_{h 1} &=600-280=320 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$ Substitute the value of $T_{h 1}=320 \mathrm{K}$ in Eq. (1), we get $320-T_{c 2}=20$ $\text{or }\quad T_{c 2}=300 \mathrm{K}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:q43-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 43
me:2015:q43-s2.question: A cylindrical uranium fuel rod of radius 5 mm in a nuclear reactor is generating heat at the rate of $4\times 10^{7} Wm^{3}$ . The rod is cooled by a liquid (convective heat transfer coefficient 1000 W/$m^{2}$-K) at  $25^{\circ}C$. At steady state, the surface temperature (in K) of the rod is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data:

$$\begin{aligned} r&=5 \mathrm{mm}=0.005 \mathrm{m}\\ \therefore \quad &=2 r=2 \times 0.005=0.010 \mathrm{m} \\ q_{G} &=4 \times 10^{7} \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ h_{0} &=1000 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \\ T_{0} &=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}$$

For steady state heat transfer,

Rate of heat generation in the rod

= rate of convection heat transfer from rod surface to fluid

$$\begin{aligned} q_{G} \times \text { volume of } \operatorname{rod} &=h_{0} A\left(T_{s}-T_{0}\right) \\ q_{G} \times \frac{\pi}{4} d^{2} l^{\prime} &=h_{0} \times \pi d l\left(T_{s}-T_{0}\right) \\ \frac{d q_{G}}{4} &=h_{0}\left(T_{s}-T_{0}\right) \\ \frac{0.010 \times 4 \times 10^{7}}{4} &=1000\left(T_{s}-25\right) \\ \text{or }\quad T_{s}-25 &=100\\ \text{or }\quad T_{s}&=100+25=125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\\ &=(125+273) \mathrm{K}=398 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:q44-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 44
me:2015:q44-s2.question: Work is done on an adiabatic system due to which its velocity changes from 10 m/s to 20 m/s, elevation increases by 20 m and temperature increases by 1 K. The mass of the system is 10 kg,  $C_{v}$  = 100 J/(kg.K) and gravitational acceleration is 10 m/$s^{2}$ . If there is no change in any other component of the energy of the system, the magnitude of total work done (in kJ) on the system is _______

primary.subtopicLabel: First Law, Heat, Work and Energy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - First Law, Heat, Work and Energy
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \delta Q&=d E+\delta W \\ 0&=\Delta U+\Delta K \cdot E+\Delta P \cdot E+\delta W \\ 0&=m c_{v} d T+\frac{1}{2} m\left(V_{2}^{2}-V_{1}^{2}\right)+m g \\ &\qquad +(z_{2}-z_{1})+\delta W\\ 0&=10 \times 0.1 \times 1+\frac{1}{2} \times 10\left((20)^{2}-(10)^{2}\right) \times 10^{-3} \\ &\qquad +10 \times 10 \times 20 \times 10^{-3}+\delta W \\ \therefore \quad \delta W&=-4.5 \mathrm{kJ} \\ &=4.5 \mathrm{kJ}, \text{work don on the system} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **4.5**.

me:2015:q45-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 45
me:2015:q45-s2.question: One kg of air (R = 287 J/kg-K) undergoes an irreversible process between equilibrium state 1      ($20^{\circ}$C, 0.9 $m^{3}$ ) and equilibrium state 2 ($20^{\circ}$C, 0.6 $m^{3}$ ). The change in entropy $s_{2}$-$s_{1}$ (in J/kg-K)    is _______

primary.subtopicLabel: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} s_{2}-s_{1} &=c_{v} \ln \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}+R \ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} \\ &=R \ln \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} \quad \because T_{1}=T_{2} \\ &=287 \ln \frac{0.6}{0.9}=-116.368 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **-116** (acceptable range: [-117, -115]).

me:2015:q46-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 46
me:2015:q46-s2.question: For the same values of peak pressure, peak temperature and heat rejection, the correct order of efficiencies for Otto, Dual and Diesel cycles is

detailed_solution.markdown:
For same peak pressure, peak temperature and heat rejection

$\eta_{Dieseal}\gt\eta_{Dual}\gt\eta_{Otto}$

For same compression ratio and heat rejection

$\eta_{Otto}\gt\eta_{Dual}\gt\eta_{Dieseal}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:q47-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 47
me:2015:q47-s2.question: In a Rankine cycle, the enthalpies at turbine entry and outlet are 3159 kJ/kg and 2187 kJ/kg, respectively. If the specific pump work is 2 kJ/kg, the specific steam consumption (in kg/kW-h) of the cycle based on net output is _______________

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} w_{\text {turbine }} &=h_{1}-h_{2} \\ &=(3159-2187) \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ w_{\text {net }} &=w_{\text {turbine }}-w_{\text {pump }} \\ &=972-2=970 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}$$ Specific steam consumption $=\frac{3600}{970} \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kWh}=3.711 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kWh}$ Specific steam consumption is amount of steam required to produce 1 kWh(or) 3600 kJ of work. Therefore, the correct answer is **3.7** (acceptable range: [3.6, 3.8]).

me:2015:q48-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 48
me:2015:q48-s2.question: A cube and a sphere made of cast iron (each of volume 1000 $cm^{3}$) were cast under identical conditions.  The time taken for solidifying the cube was 4 s. The solidification time (in s) for the sphere is __________

detailed_solution.markdown:
Time of solidification(T)

$$\begin{array}{l} =k\left[\frac{\text { volume }}{\text { surface area }}\right]^{2} \\ {\left[\begin{array}{l} \left.\frac{T_{\text {sphere }}}{T_{\text {cube }}}\right]=\left[\frac{A_{\text {cube }}}{A_{\text {sphere }}}\right]^{2}=\left[\frac{6 a^{2}}{4 / 3 \pi r^{3}}\right]^{2}-(1) \end{array}\right.}\\ \because\left[V_{\text {sphere }}=V_{\text {cube }}\right] \\ V_{\text {cube }}=a^{3}=1000 \mathrm{cm}^{3} \\ \therefore \qquad a =10\mathrm{cm}\\ V_{\text {sphere }}=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}=1000\\ \Rightarrow \qquad r=6.2035 \mathrm{cm} \\ \end{array}$$

Putting in Eq.(1), we get

$\frac{T_{\text {sphere }}}{T_{\text {cube }}}=\left[\frac{6 \times 10^{2}}{4 \pi \times(6.2035)^{2}}\right]^{2}$

$T_{\text {sphere }} =6.157355 \mathrm{seconds}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **6.15** (acceptable range: [6, 6.3]).

me:2015:q49-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 49
me:2015:q49-s2.question: In a two-stage wire drawing operation, the fractional reduction (ratio of change in cross-sectional area to initial cross-sectional area) in the first stage is 0.4. The fractional reduction in the second stage is 0.3. The overall fractional reduction is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Fractional reduction in first stage

$=\frac{\text { Change in area in first stage }}{\text { Original area }(A) \text { before reduction }}$

$0.4=\frac{\text { Change in area in first stage }}{A}$

Change in area in first stage $=0.4 \mathrm{A}$

Area after first redirection $=A-0.4 A=0.6 A$

Fraction reduction in second stage

$$\begin{array}{l} =\frac{\text { Change in area in second stage }}{\text { Original area before second stage }} \\ 0.3=\frac{\text { Change in area in second stage }}{0.6 \mathrm{A}} \end{array}$$

Change in after 2 nd stage $=0.18 A$

Remaining area after 2nd reduction

$$\begin{array}{l} =0.60 .18 \mathrm{A} \\ =0.42 \mathrm{A} \end{array}$$

Overall reduction in area

$=A-0.42 A=0.58 A$

Overall fractional reduction

$$\begin{array}{l} =\frac{\text { Overall reduction in area }}{\text { Original area }} \\ =\frac{0.58 \mathrm{A}}{\mathrm{A}}=0.58 \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:q50-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 50
me:2015:q50-s2.question:
The flow stress (in MPa) of a material is given by
$\sigma=500\varepsilon^{0.1}$ ;

where $\varepsilon$ is true strain. The Young's modulus of elasticity of the material is 200 GPa. A block of thickness 100 mm made of this material is compressed to 95 mm thickness and then the load is removed. The final dimension of the block (in mm) is _________

detailed_solution.markdown:
Equating the stress to the equation up to elastic limit, we get

$$\begin{aligned} \sigma &=500 \varepsilon^{0.1}=200 \times 10^{3} \times \varepsilon \\ \Rightarrow \qquad\varepsilon^{0.9} &=\frac{500}{200 \times 10^{3}}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \varepsilon(\text { tuestain })&=1.28476 \times 10^{-3}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \varepsilon_{T}&=\ln (1+\varepsilon)\\ \varepsilon(\text { engg.strain })_{\text {upto elastic limit }}&=1.285586 \times 10^{-3}=\frac{\Delta L}{L} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad(\Delta L)_{\text {upto elastic limit }}&=0.128558 \mathrm{mm}\\ \Rightarrow \qquad & \text{Final dimension of block} \\ &=95+ \text{ elastic recover}\\ &=95.128558 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **95.17** (acceptable range: [95.14, 95.2]).

me:2015:q51-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 51
me:2015:q51-s2.question: During a TIG welding process, the arc current and arc voltage were 50 A and 60 V, respectively, when the welding speed was 150 mm/min. me:2015:q52-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 52
me:2015:q52-s2.question: A single point cutting tool with $0^{\circ}$ rake angle is used in an orthogonal machining process. At a cutting speed of 180 m/min, the thrust force is 490 N. If the coefficient of friction between the tool and the chip is 0.7, then the power consumption (in kW) for the machining operation is ________

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \frac{F}{N}&=\frac{F_{T}}{F_{C}}=0.7\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{490}{F_{C}} &=0.7 \\ F_{C} &=700 \mathrm{N} \\ \text { Power } &=F_{C} \times V=\frac{700 \times 180}{60} \\ &=2.1 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **2.1** (acceptable range: [2, 2.2]).

me:2015:q53-s2.title: GATE ME 2015 | Set 2 | Question: 53
me:2015:q53-s2.question: A resistance-capacitance relaxation circuit is used in an electrical discharge machining process. The discharge voltage is 100 V. At a spark cycle time of 25 $\mu$s, the average power input required is  1 kW. The capacitance (in $\mu$F) in the circuit is

detailed_solution.concept: Manufacturing Engineering - Machining and Machine Tool Operation

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

me:2015:ga:q10-s2.question:
